source_span: We interpret this as effectively signaling a hawkish bias, with the intent of keeping December as a live option for the Committee's next hike. We continue to expect a hike at the December FOMC meeting.
source_chain: The statement's new 'accumulation of more information' sentence signals a hawkish bias meant to keep December live, therefore JPM still expects a December hike; but the press conference gave no clear rationale for the pause, therefore the market came away less convinced a December tightening plan exists. Invalidation: JPM gives no clean conditional break, only diminished conviction from the vague presser.
pulse_chain: The statement's new line upgrades the Fed's posture, therefore JPMorgan reads it as a deliberate hawkish bias to keep December alive and still expects a hike then; but Warsh gave no clear economic rationale in the press conference, therefore JPMorgan says the market came out less convinced the Committee has a December plan. Invalidation (for the theme as a whole, not JPM's own): a firm core PCE print keeps the hawks' December case, a soft one prices the first dovish mistake of this chair's tenure.
why: The pulse reproduces JPMorgan's exact two-step argument (hawkish statement language → bias to keep December live, still expects a hike / vague press conference → market less convinced) with correct attribution and unreversed direction, even though it folds in other banks' separate debates and supplies its own closing invalidation.
